---
title: "Installation and development setup"
---

For research use, follow the [package quickstart](../package/quickstart.qmd).
It creates a uv project and selects a PyTorch build for your machine. Python
and Hydra call the same installed library; a source checkout is not required.

For development, install uv and Git, then:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/OJWatson/metis.git
cd metis
uv sync --locked --all-extras
uv run --locked --all-extras pytest
uv run --locked --all-extras ruff check src tests
uv run --locked --all-extras ty check src
uv build
```

The checkout selects CPU PyTorch on Linux/Windows and the platform build on
Apple Silicon macOS. Intel Macs are unsupported by the current PyTorch range.
The environment is `.venv`; manual activation is unnecessary. Keep
`--all-extras` on checkout commands so synchronization retains optional features.

For CUDA, select a compatible named PyTorch index following the quickstart,
update the local lockfile, then synchronize all extras again. Dependencies do
not configure GPU drivers. GPU support is tested separately from CPU checks.

Select the project's `.venv` Python in a notebook interface. The Quarto CLI is
installed separately; its Python dependencies are included in the docs extra.
See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/OJWatson/metis/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for distribution, notebook and automated handoff checks.

Old source-checkout commands and raw checkpoints are explained in the
[migration guide](../package/migration.qmd); they are not the current API.
